rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; i8863 p. 3, Who cannot claim a credit: "5. The student has not been issued a TIN by the due date of his or her 2025 return (including extensions)", and Student qualifications: "5. Filers and students must have been issued a TIN by the due date of their 2025 return (including extensions)." i8863 p. 2: "You may be able to claim an education credit if you, your spouse, or a dependent you claim on your tax return was a student enrolled at or attending an eligible educational institution." The reply changed: its student gate now also requires person.sav_claimed no ("1. You're claimed as a dependent on another person's tax return", a filer test the project applies once for the return at f8863.eligible through sli.claimed). It still tests person.tin without person.itin_applied, which the project accepts (p970 p. 11: "If an ATIN or ITIN is applied for on or before the due date of a 2025 return (including extensions) and the IRS issues an ATIN or ITIN as a result of the application, the IRS will consider the ATIN or ITIN as issued on or before the due date of the return"; ruled in round 1), so by reading a student whose ITIN was applied for by the due date and issued gets no credit (no such record in the sample); and it still omits f8863.paid, the return-level screen that precedes person.edu, so the candidate-unknown records are returns with f8863.paid no, where the interview never asks the student's answers (classm.f2441.1.deepseek to .5), together with sav_claimed and tin where they are not asked. It reads person.tin and person.edu_1098t as the project does, so the reworded questions (BUG-0225, BUG-0226) change neither side. The worksheet arithmetic is the project's aqee definition. The 2 value records (generated 32, $3,541.94 against $0.00, and generated 102, $4,000.00 against $0.00; refused) supply sav_claimed yes with sa.dependent no, a record the interview does not produce (sav_claimed is asked only after sa.dependent yes; checked on each witness): representation on that kind. The project-unknown record is a partial of classm.dependent.7.deepseek withholding edu_line25, where the candidate's sav_claimed yes gives zero first. Lines 27 to 30 also omit the filers' TIN test (household.all_tin, amb.2025.edu_filer_tin, owner decision D7(a)); no record isolates it. rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; i8863 p. 3, Who cannot claim a credit: "5. The student has not been issued a TIN by the due date of his or her 2025 return (including extensions)", and Student qualifications: "5. Filers and students must have been issued a TIN by the due date of their 2025 return (including extensions)." i8863 p. 2: "You may be able to claim an education credit if you, your spouse, or a dependent you claim on your tax return was a student enrolled at or attending an eligible educational institution." Same expression as round 1. The candidate omits the student-TIN test of edu_student (person.tin or person.itin_applied; p970 p. 11 treats an ITIN applied for by the due date and issued as issued by then) and f8863.paid, the return-level screen that precedes person.edu; lines 27 to 30 also omit the filers' TIN test (household.all_tin, amb.2025.edu_filer_tin, owner decision D7(a)). The partial of classm.f8863.4.deepseek withholding person.tin shows it: the project needs the TIN, the candidate gives $4,000.00. The candidate-unknown records are returns with f8863.paid no, where the interview never asks the student's answers (classm.f2441.1.deepseek to .5): its refusal declaration on person.edu_over is read before anything else, and with no expenses paid for anyone there is no student (the quoted p. 2 sentence), so it requires an answer the source does not need. Its edu_over refusal matches the reworded question (BUG-0197). The worksheet arithmetic (expenses less lines 2a to 2c, floored at zero; capped at $4,000; less $2,000; 25%; line 30 rule) is the project's aqee definition. Triage executable-triage-v2 (triage/person.json; 1,325 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 1,792 partial records): 1,694 of 4,395 comparisons agree; 2,700 candidate-unknown, 1 project-unknown; on returns the full interview completes: 1,155 candidate-unknown.

The worksheet arithmetic is the project's aqee definition. Lines 27 to 30 also omit the filers' TIN test (household.all_tin, amb.2025.edu_filer_tin, owner decision D7(a)); no record in the sample isolates it this round. rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; i8863 p. 3, Who cannot claim a credit: "5. The student has not been issued a TIN by the due date of his or her 2025 return (including extensions)", and Student qualifications: "5. Filers and students must have been issued a TIN by the due date of their 2025 return (including extensions)." i8863 p. 2: "You may be able to claim an education credit if you, your spouse, or a dependent you claim on your tax return was a student enrolled at or attending an eligible educational institution." The reply changed: its student gate now also requires person.sav_claimed no ("1. You're claimed as a dependent on another person's tax return", a filer test the project applies once for the return at f8863.eligible through sli.claimed). It still tests person.tin without person.itin_applied, which the project accepts (p970 p. 11: "If an ATIN or ITIN is applied for on or before the due date of a 2025 return (including extensions) and the IRS issues an ATIN or ITIN as a result of the application, the IRS will consider the ATIN or ITIN as issued on or before the due date of the return"; ruled in round 1), so by reading a student whose ITIN was applied for by the due date and issued gets no credit (no such record in the sample); and it still omits f8863.paid, the return-level screen that precedes person.edu, so the candidate-unknown records are returns with f8863.paid no, where the interview never asks the student's answers (classm.f2441.1.deepseek to .5), together with sav_claimed and tin where they are not asked. It reads person.tin and person.edu_1098t as the project does, so the reworded questions (BUG-0225, BUG-0226) change neither side. The worksheet arithmetic is the project's aqee definition. The 2 value records (generated 32, $3,541.94 against $0.00, and generated 102, $4,000.00 against $0.00; refused) supply sav_claimed yes with sa.dependent no, a record the interview does not produce (sav_claimed is asked only after sa.dependent yes; checked on each witness): representation on that kind. The project-unknown record is a partial of classm.dependent.7.deepseek withholding edu_line25, where the candidate's sav_claimed yes gives zero first. Lines 27 to 30 also omit the filers' TIN test (household.all_tin, amb.2025.edu_filer_tin, owner decision D7(a)); no record isolates it. Triage executable-triage-v2 (triage/person.json; 1,382 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 2,014 partial records; every witness listed by a scratch rerun of tools/transcription/triage.mjs with the witness cap lifted): 2,371 of 4,711 comparisons agree; 2 value, 1 project-unknown, 2,337 candidate-unknown; on returns the full interview completes: 922 candidate-unknown.

The student has not been issued a TIN by the due date of his or her 2025 return (including extensions)", and Student qualifications: "5. Filers and students must have been issued a TIN by the due date of their 2025 return (including extensions)." i8863 p. 2: "You may be able to claim an education credit if you, your spouse, or a dependent you claim on your tax return was a student enrolled at or attending an eligible educational institution." The reply changed: the student-TIN test is now person.tin, but without person.itin_applied, which the project accepts (p970 p. 11: "If an ATIN or ITIN is applied for on or before the due date of a 2025 return (including extensions) and the IRS issues an ATIN or ITIN as a result of the application, the IRS will consider the ATIN or ITIN as issued on or before the due date of the return"; ruled in round 1); by reading, a student whose ITIN was applied for by the due date and issued gets no credit from the candidate (no such record in the sample). It still omits f8863.paid, the return-level screen that precedes person.edu, so the candidate-unknown records are returns with f8863.paid no, where the interview never asks the student's answers (classm.f2441.1.deepseek to .5): its refusal declaration on person.edu_over is read first, an answer the source does not need when no expenses were paid for anyone (the quoted p. 2 sentence). Generated 47 (round 2's candidate-shows-skipped, the taxpayer with no TIN) now agrees. Its edu_over refusal matches the reworded question (BUG-0197). The worksheet arithmetic is the project's aqee definition. Lines 27 to 30 also omit the filers' TIN test (household.all_tin, amb.2025.edu_filer_tin, owner decision D7(a)); no record in the sample isolates it this round. Lines 28 to 30 carry no refusal declaration, so on stage19.refuse.period_over_person the project refuses at edu_over_refused and the candidate shows an amount on a return its own line 27 refuses: scope on that kind. Railroad retirement (tier 1) compensation on line 8a is refused for a person with a Schedule C (person.se_rrta), so line 8a is W-2 boxes 3 and 7 on both sides. Both use this person's own Schedule SE line 13 (Pub. 560 p. 39, Step 2).

Candidate refusals and unknowns are its se_screen and rrta placement, ruled at person.se_line6 (classm.f5695.2 se_screen true with no Schedule C; classm.tcw.6 rrta true, which the project refuses at person.credit). rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; i2441 p. 4, Lines 4 and 5: "If filing jointly, figure your and your spouse's earned income separately" and "Earned income for figuring the credit generally includes the following amounts. 1. The amount shown on Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR, line 1z"; amb.2025.dc_line1e_attribution (owner ruling: line 1e is the earned income of the spouse whose Forms W-2 show box 10; with both, refused while a credit remains, otherwise shown once on the taxpayer's line 4). The reply changed in two places: its line 1e part now reads f1040.line1e (fix round 3's read f2441.line26, which line 1e copies when benefits are reported), and its self-employment part is on sc.result again (fix round 3's at-risk kind is gone). As in fix round 3, where both spouses' Forms W-2 show box 10 it adds the whole of line 1e to each spouse (person.h_dc_1e), counting line 1z's line 1e twice, which no reading of the register allows; no record in the sample isolates it (the project refuses such a return at f2441.attrib_gate while a credit remains). No value differs on the sample. The project refusals are cited Form 2441 and return screens reached through the line (f2441.line14_bad on classm.w2.1.deepseek and stage15.refuse.f2441.line14_over, f2441.plans_differ, sa.excluded_income on classm.f8889.5 and .5.deepseek; refused returns). The candidate-unknown records also include W-2 box 10 asked where the interview does not ask it (37 on completed returns; box 10 is asked with Form 2441): placement. The candidate declares refusals on person.se_screen and person.rrta for every person; the project asks se_screen (and, through the Schedule C, the railroad question) only of a person with a Schedule C, so every candidate-unknown record is a person with no Schedule C where the interview does not ask se_screen (classm.f2441.1.deepseek to .5, completed), and every candidate refusal supplies se_screen or rrta true for such a person (classm.f5695.2, classm.f5695.2.deepseek and classm.ssb.5 on completed returns; classm.carloan.2, classm.f8959.1, classm.w2.1 and generated returns on refused returns), an answer the interview does not produce for that person: placement (checked on every witness in the scratch rerun: none has a Schedule C). Fix round 4 re-check: the only project change since fix round 3 is BUG-0259 (person.itin_applied now counts an application to renew an expired ITIN), which this line does not read. Triage executable-triage-v2 (triage/person.json; 1,390 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 2,014 partial records; every witness listed by a scratch rerun of tools/transcription/triage.mjs with the witness cap lifted): 3,101 of 4,724 comparisons agree; 5 project-refuses, 23 candidate-refuses, 1,595 candidate-unknown; on returns the full interview completes: 3 candidate-refuses, 766 candidate-unknown.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; i2441 p. 4, Lines 4 and 5: "If filing jointly, figure your and your spouse's earned income separately" and "Earned income for figuring the credit generally includes the following amounts. 1. The amount shown on Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR, line 1z"; amb.2025.dc_line1e_attribution (owner ruling: line 1e is the earned income of the spouse whose Forms W-2 show box 10; with both, refused while a credit remains, otherwise shown once on the taxpayer's line 4). The reply changed: it now adds f2441.line26 (line 1e) for a person with a Form W-2 showing box 10, which fixes fix round 2's model error (classm.carloan.1 no longer differs), and its self-employment part is on sc.line31 again. But where both spouses' Forms W-2 show box 10 it adds the whole of line 26 to each spouse, counting line 1z's line 1e twice, which no reading of the register allows; no record in the sample isolates it (the project refuses such a return at f2441.attrib_gate while a credit remains, so the doubled amount reaches only printed lines 4 and 5 where none remains). No value differs on the sample. The project refusals are cited Form 2441 and return screens reached through the line (f2441.line14_bad on classm.w2.1.deepseek and stage15.refuse.f2441.line14_over, f2441.plans_differ, sa.excluded_income on classm.f8889.5 and .5.deepseek, sc not_at_risk on stage14.refuse.at_risk; refused returns). The candidate-unknown records also include W-2 box 10 asked where the interview does not ask it (classm.f8995.2, classm.sc.4, completed; box 10 is asked with Form 2441): placement. The candidate declares refusals on person.se_screen and person.rrta for every person; the project asks se_screen (and, through the Schedule C, the railroad question) only of a person with a Schedule C, so every candidate-unknown record is a person with no Schedule C where the interview does not ask se_screen (classm.f2441.1.deepseek to .5, completed), and every candidate refusal supplies se_screen true for such a person (classm.f5695.2, classm.f5695.2.deepseek and classm.ssb.5 on completed returns; classm.carloan.2, classm.f8959.1 and generated returns such as 8, 11 and 16 on refused returns), an answer the interview does not produce for that person: placement (checked on every witness: none has a Schedule C). Fix round 3 re-check: the only project change since fix round 2 is BUG-0256 (person.tin: an expired ITIN counts only if renewed by the due date), which this line does not read. Triage executable-triage-v2 (triage/person.json; 1,390 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 2,014 partial records; every witness listed by a scratch rerun of tools/transcription/triage.mjs with the witness cap lifted): 3,128 of 4,724 comparisons agree; 6 project-refuses, 16 candidate-refuses, 1,574 candidate-unknown; on returns the full interview completes: 3 candidate-refuses, 766 candidate-unknown.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained (as the prior ruling). Box 1 is the same on both sides. Line 1e goes to the only person whose Forms W-2 show box 10, or to the taxpayer when nobody's do, on both sides; when both spouses' do, the second now gives it to neither (and refuses, its h_dc_1e_split), where the project follows the binding reading amb.2025.dc_line1e_attribution (owner decision 6): shown in the taxpayer's line 4 and refused when a credit remains (f2441.attrib_gate). The self-employment part is the same on returns the tool completes: the second subtracts the Schedule SE deduction without a Schedule C guard (zero below the $400 floor, so the Schedule C result is used, as the project does when no Schedule SE is filed) and leaves out statutory employee income, which is refused on each Schedule C (sc.statutory). i2441 p. 4, Lines 4 and 5, "If filing jointly, figure your and your spouse's earned income separately".

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. Box 1 and the self-employment part are the same on both sides: the self-employment part differs only as person.eic_se does (the project's zero for a person with no Schedule C against the second's $400 floor, and the second's exclusion of statutory employee income, which is refused by sc.statutory), and both use Schedule C profit or loss when no Schedule SE is filed (p503 p. 11, Self-employment earnings, "Include your self-employment earnings in earned income, even if they are less than $400 and you didn't file Schedule SE"). Line 1e goes to the only person on a return that is not joint and to the one spouse whose Forms W-2 show box 10 on both sides. The sides differ only when both spouses' Forms W-2 show box 10: the second counts line 1e in both spouses' earned income, so it counts it twice; the project follows the binding reading amb.2025.dc_line1e_attribution (owner decision 6), refusing when line 1e is above zero and a credit remains (f2441.attrib_gate) and otherwise showing it in the taxpayer's line 4, where it cannot change the credit. i2441 p. 4, Lines 4 and 5, "If filing jointly, figure your and your spouse's earned income separately".

The reply is the Schedule C total less its person.se_line13 for everyone, the project's amount wherever both evaluate; no value differs. Its unknowns are those of person.se_line13: The candidate binds the Schedule SE definition to this person's Schedule C total and person.wages (W-2 boxes 3 and 7) for every person, without the project's Schedule C condition (person.has_sc); for a person with no Schedule C the amount is zero in both graphs, but the candidate still reads W-2 box 3 for Schedule SE line 8a. Every candidate-unknown record is such a person (checked on each witness: none has a Schedule C) with a Form W-2 whose box 3 the interview never asked, because no line of the project's return needs it there (stage21.t068.no_business_no_carryover on a completed return; stage16.cleanup.f5695_no_audit, f5695_no_section_b, f5695_small_wind and mut.clwb_two_children; stage16.cleanup.refuse.f2441_line24, ss.early.refusal and stage21.t068.orphan_with_wages_refused refused): an answer the source does not need to determine the result. The reply's fix-round-4 se_screen and rrta placements are gone: its refusal now applies only with a Schedule C. The 2 candidate refusals are partials of classm.g28.2.deepseek withholding the spouse's se_screen or rrta (a person with a Schedule C, where both sides need the answer; the project is unknown, the candidate's refusal declaration reads the withheld answer; refused return). The reply's note is new; its expression is unchanged. Hardening round re-check: the only project change since fix round 4 is BUG-0263 (person.sep_s3 now links amb.2025.sep_loss_floor; no value change), which this line does not read. rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. The project enters zero for a person with no Schedule C; the second applies the $400 floor of Schedule SE line 4c, which gives zero for the same person. Otherwise the same Schedule SE computation; church employee income, the optional methods and statutory employee income are refused (person.se_screen, sc.statutory), so the second's sums over all of the person's Schedules C (it no longer excludes statutory employee income) select the same entries as the project's. Railroad retirement (tier 1) compensation on line 8a is refused for a person with a Schedule C (person.se_rrta), so line 8a is W-2 boxes 3 and 7 on both sides. EIC Worksheet B Part 1 for a person filing Schedule SE and Part 2 otherwise on both sides (i1040gi p. 47).

rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; Form 8606 (2025), Part I: with no 2025 distribution, "Enter the amount from line 3 on line 14". As before the reply writes line 14 as its nondeductible amount plus its Form 8606 line 2 (line 3) and refuses a distribution at its ira_dist_gate, the same two amounts as the project's, but it drops the person.sav_trad gate that fix round 2's reply had (and the project has, person.ira_has), so for a person who made no traditional IRA contribution it still needs the worksheet's answers (ira_basis, ira_dist, ira_work_plan, ira_excess, plan, plan_screen and se_screen). Of the candidate-unknown records on completed returns, checked on each witness, 873 are persons who answered sav_trad no, where the interview does not ask those questions (classm.f2441.1.deepseek, classm.f8995.2, stage15.f8880.s2) (the other 26 are contributors, stage16.ira.i1 to i10, asked plan, plan_screen, se_screen or eligible_educator where the interview does not ask them: placement, as in fix round 2); for such a person the amount is zero whatever the answers (i1040gi p. 95, Line 20: "If you made contributions to a traditional IRA for 2025, you may be able to take an IRA deduction."), so the reply requires answers the source does not need to determine the result. No value differs. Candidate refusals are those of person.ira_deduction; project refusals are the cited Pub. 590-A refusals. Fix round 3 re-check: the only project change since fix round 2 is BUG-0256 (person.tin: an expired ITIN counts only if renewed by the due date), which this line does not read. rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; Form 8606 (2025), Part I: with no 2025 distribution, "Enter the amount from line 3 on line 14". The reply copies its Form 8606 line 3 (nondeductible amount plus line 2) and refuses a distribution at its ira_dist_gate, the same amounts as the project's, but through those lines for a person who made no traditional contribution it still needs the worksheet's answers (ira_dist, ira_basis, ira_basis_adjusted, ira_excess, ira_age50, ira_work_plan, plan and plan details); the project gates the line on person.ira_has. Every candidate-unknown record on a completed return (199, checked on each witness) is a person who answered sav_trad no, where the interview does not ask those questions (for example classm.f8995.3, classm.s179.2, stage14.sc.basic, and partials withholding them); for such a person the amount is zero whatever the answers (i1040gi p. 95, Line 20: "If you made contributions to a traditional IRA for 2025, you may be able to take an IRA deduction."), so the reply requires answers the source does not need to determine the result. No value differs. The candidate refusals are other forms' refusals reached through its worksheet for persons with no contribution (mostly a spouse's scveh low_use, s179.multi, scope.other_income, sd.other_forms; refused returns) and its h_se_refused and h_plan_refused declarations; the project refusals are the cited Pub. 590-A refusals (ira.both_kinds, ira.kbh_short, person.ira_over_limit, person.ira_excess_gate, ira.over_comp, ira.special_gate and others on stage16.refuse.*; p590a p. 35). Hardening round re-check: the only project change since fix round 4 is BUG-0263 (person.sep_s3 now links amb.2025.sep_loss_floor; no value change), which this line does not read. Triage executable-triage-v2 (triage/person.json; 1,394 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 2,014 partial records; every witness listed by a scratch rerun of tools/transcription/triage.mjs with the witness cap lifted, counts identical to the record): 2,463 of 4,728 comparisons agree; 11 project-refuses, 245 candidate-refuses, 2,009 candidate-unknown; on returns the full interview completes: 199 candidate-unknown.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; Form 8606 (2025), Part I: with no 2025 distribution, "Enter the amount from line 3 on line 14". As before the reply writes line 14 as its nondeductible amount plus its Form 8606 line 2 (line 3) and refuses a distribution at its ira_dist_gate, the same two amounts as the project's, but through those lines it still needs the worksheet and basis answers for a person who made no traditional contribution (ira_basis, ira_basis_adjusted, ira_dist, ira_work_plan, ira_excess, plan, plan_screen and se_screen). Of the candidate-unknown records on completed returns, checked on each witness in a scratch rerun, 899 are persons who answered sav_trad no, where the interview does not ask those questions (classm.f2441.1.deepseek, classm.f8995.2, stage15.f8880.s2) (the other 26 are contributors, stage16.ira.i1 to i10, asked plan, plan_screen, se_screen or eligible_educator where the interview does not ask them: placement); for such a person the amount is zero whatever the answers (i1040gi p. 95, Line 20: "If you made contributions to a traditional IRA for 2025, you may be able to take an IRA deduction."), so the reply requires answers the source does not need to determine the result. No value differs. The candidate refusals are other forms' refusals reached through its worksheet for persons with no contribution (scveh low_use, s179.multi, s1.alimony_unsupported; refused returns) and its se_screen placements (classm.f5695.2 and classm.ssb.5 on completed returns); the project refusals are the cited Pub. 590-A refusals (ira.both_kinds, ira.kbh_short, person.ira_over_limit, ira.over_comp, ira.special_gate, person.ira_dist_gate on stage16.refuse.*; p590a p. 35). Fix round 4 re-check: the only project change since fix round 3 is BUG-0259 (person.itin_applied now counts an application to renew an expired ITIN), which this line does not read. Triage executable-triage-v2 (triage/person.json; 1,390 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 2,014 partial records; every witness listed by a scratch rerun of tools/transcription/triage.mjs with the witness cap lifted): 2,395 of 4,724 comparisons agree; 11 project-refuses, 270 candidate-refuses, 2,048 candidate-unknown; on returns the full interview completes: 3 candidate-refuses, 925 candidate-unknown.

The reply changed: it now gates the basis on its Form 8606 filer test (basis with a distribution, or nondeductible contributions), and through its person.ira_nondeductible it drops the person.sav_trad gate that fix round 2's reply had (and the project has, person.ira_has), so for a person who made no traditional IRA contribution it still needs the worksheet's answers (ira_basis, ira_basis_adjusted, ira_dist, ira_work_plan, ira_excess, plan, plan_screen and se_screen). Of the candidate-unknown records on completed returns, checked on each witness, 873 are persons who answered sav_trad no, where the interview does not ask those questions (classm.f2441.1.deepseek, classm.f8995.2, stage15.f8880.s2) (the other 26 are contributors, stage16.ira.i1 to i10, asked plan, plan_screen, se_screen or eligible_educator where the interview does not ask them: placement, as in fix round 2); for such a person the amount is zero whatever the answers (i1040gi p. 95, Line 20: "If you made contributions to a traditional IRA for 2025, you may be able to take an IRA deduction."), so the reply requires answers the source does not need to determine the result. No value differs. Candidate refusals are those of person.ira_deduction; project refusals are the cited Pub. 590-A refusals (stage16.refuse.ira.both_kinds, kbh_short, person.ira_excess, over_limit). Fix round 3 re-check: the only project change since fix round 2 is BUG-0256 (person.tin: an expired ITIN counts only if renewed by the due date), which this line does not read. Triage executable-triage-v2 (triage/person.json; 1,390 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 2,014 partial records; every witness listed by a scratch rerun of tools/transcription/triage.mjs with the witness cap lifted): 2,518 of 4,724 comparisons agree; 11 project-refuses, 231 candidate-refuses, 1,964 candidate-unknown; on returns the full interview completes: 3 candidate-refuses, 899 candidate-unknown.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; i1040gi p. 98: "On line 12a, enter the smallest of line 7a, 10, or 11a ... This is the most you can deduct." The reply changed: it drops the person.sav_trad gate that fix round 2's reply had (and the project has, person.ira_has), so for a person who made no traditional IRA contribution it still needs the worksheet's answers (ira_work_plan, ira_excess, ira_age50, plan, plan_screen, se_screen and the self-employment capital answer). Of the candidate-unknown records on completed returns, checked on each witness, 873 are persons who answered sav_trad no, where the interview does not ask those questions (classm.f2441.1.deepseek, classm.f8995.2, stage15.f8880.s2) (the other 26 are contributors, stage16.ira.i1 to i10, asked plan, plan_screen, se_screen or eligible_educator where the interview does not ask them: placement, as in fix round 2); for such a person the amount is zero whatever the answers (i1040gi p. 95, Line 20: "If you made contributions to a traditional IRA for 2025, you may be able to take an IRA deduction."), so the reply requires answers the source does not need to determine the result. Where the person contributes, the smallest of its line 7, ira.line10 and person.ira_contrib is the project's ira_line12; no value differs. The 231 candidate refusals are other forms' refusals reached through its worksheet for persons with no contribution (scveh low_use on classm.g28.2 and .2.deepseek, s179.multi, ho_both_limits, s1.alimony_unsupported; refused returns) and its se_screen, plan_screen and railroad placements (classm.f5695.2 and classm.ssb.5 on completed returns); the 11 project refusals are the cited Pub. 590-A refusals (ira.both_kinds, ira.kbh_short, person.ira_over_limit, ira.over_comp, ira.special_gate, ira.excl_gate, ira.combat_gate, person.ira_dist_gate, ira.cov_gate on stage16.refuse.*; p590a p. 35). Fix round 3 re-check: the only project change since fix round 2 is BUG-0256 (person.tin: an expired ITIN counts only if renewed by the due date), which this line does not read. rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; i1040gi p. 98: "On line 12a, enter the smallest of line 7a, 10, or 11a ... This is the most you can deduct." The reply changed in form: the smaller of its line 7, ira.line10 and person.ira_contrib, with the person.sav_trad gate now inside person.ira_contrib (zero for a person who made no traditional contribution). But the smaller-of still evaluates its line 7 and line 10 for that person, so it still needs the worksheet's answers (ira_work_plan, ira_excess, plan, plan_screen, se_screen and the self-employment capital answer), as in fix round 3; the project gates the whole line on person.ira_has. Of the candidate-unknown records on completed returns, checked on each witness in a scratch rerun, 875 are persons who answered sav_trad no, where the interview does not ask those questions (classm.f2441.1.deepseek, classm.f8995.2, stage15.f8880.s2) (the other 26 are contributors, stage16.ira.i1 to i10, asked plan, plan_screen, se_screen or eligible_educator where the interview does not ask them: placement); for such a person the amount is zero whatever the answers (i1040gi p. 95, Line 20: "If you made contributions to a traditional IRA for 2025, you may be able to take an IRA deduction."), so the reply requires answers the source does not need to determine the result. No value differs. The candidate refusals are other forms' refusals reached through its worksheet for persons with no contribution (scveh low_use, s179.multi, s1.alimony_unsupported; refused returns) and its se_screen placements (classm.f5695.2 and classm.ssb.5 on completed returns); the project refusals are the cited Pub. 590-A refusals (ira.both_kinds, ira.kbh_short, person.ira_over_limit, ira.over_comp, ira.special_gate, person.ira_dist_gate on stage16.refuse.*; p590a p. 35). Fix round 4 re-check: the only project change since fix round 3 is BUG-0259 (person.itin_applied now counts an application to renew an expired ITIN), which this line does not read. rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; f8606 (2025) Part I: "In 2025, did you take a distribution from a traditional IRA, or make a Roth IRA conversion?" The reply writes the gate as its Form 8606 filer test and a distribution, as in fix round 2, but its filer test reads person.ira_nondeductible, and like that line it drops the person.sav_trad gate that fix round 2's reply had (and the project has, person.ira_has), so for a person who made no traditional IRA contribution it still needs the worksheet's answers (ira_basis, ira_dist, ira_work_plan, ira_excess, plan, plan_screen and se_screen). Of the candidate-unknown records on completed returns, checked on each witness, all 805 are persons who answered sav_trad no, where the interview does not ask those questions (classm.f2441.1.deepseek, classm.f8995.2, stage15.f8880.s2); for such a person the amount is zero whatever the answers (i1040gi p. 95, Line 20: "If you made contributions to a traditional IRA for 2025, you may be able to take an IRA deduction."), so the reply requires answers the source does not need to determine the result. No value differs. Candidate refusals are those of person.ira_deduction; project refusals are the cited Pub. 590-A refusals. Fix round 3 re-check: the only project change since fix round 2 is BUG-0256 (person.tin: an expired ITIN counts only if renewed by the due date), which this line does not read. Triage executable-triage-v2 (triage/person.json; 1,390 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 2,014 partial records; every witness listed by a scratch rerun of tools/transcription/triage.mjs with the witness cap lifted): 2,770 of 4,724 comparisons agree; 10 project-refuses, 231 candidate-refuses, 1,713 candidate-unknown; on returns the full interview completes: 3 candidate-refuses, 805 candidate-unknown.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; f8606 (2025) Part I: "In 2025, did you take a distribution from a traditional IRA, or make a Roth IRA conversion?" Same expression as fix round 3 apart from form: its Form 8606 filer test and a distribution; its filer test reads person.ira_nondeductible, so for a person who made no traditional contribution it still needs the worksheet's answers (ira_basis, ira_dist, ira_work_plan, ira_excess, plan, plan_screen and se_screen). rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; i8606 p. 2, Who Must File: "You made nondeductible contributions to a traditional IRA for 2025" and "You received distributions from a traditional IRA in 2025 and your basis in these IRAs is more than zero." The reply tests both conditions as before (the project screens a distribution with basis at retirement.special), but it drops the person.sav_trad gate that fix round 2's reply had (and the project has, person.ira_has), so for a person who made no traditional IRA contribution it still needs the worksheet's answers (ira_work_plan, ira_excess, ira_basis, ira_dist, plan, plan_screen and se_screen). Of the candidate-unknown records on completed returns, checked on each witness, 873 are persons who answered sav_trad no, where the interview does not ask those questions (classm.f2441.1.deepseek, classm.f8995.2, stage15.f8880.s2) (the other 26 are contributors, stage16.ira.i1 to i10, asked plan, plan_screen, se_screen or eligible_educator where the interview does not ask them: placement, as in fix round 2); for such a person the amount is zero whatever the answers (i1040gi p. 95, Line 20: "If you made contributions to a traditional IRA for 2025, you may be able to take an IRA deduction."), so the reply requires answers the source does not need to determine the result. No value differs. Candidate refusals are those of person.ira_deduction; project refusals are the cited Pub. 590-A refusals. Fix round 3 re-check: the only project change since fix round 2 is BUG-0256 (person.tin: an expired ITIN counts only if renewed by the due date), which this line does not read. rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; i8606 p. 2, Who Must File: "You made nondeductible contributions to a traditional IRA for 2025" and "You received distributions from a traditional IRA in 2025 and your basis in these IRAs is more than zero." The reply tests both conditions (the project screens a distribution with basis at retirement.special), but through person.ira_nondeductible for a person who made no traditional contribution it still needs the worksheet's answers (ira_excess, ira_age50, ira_work_plan, plan, plan details and eligible_educator); the project gates the line on person.ira_has. Every candidate-unknown record on a completed return (175, checked on each witness) is a person who answered sav_trad no, where the interview does not ask those questions (for example classm.f8995.3, classm.s179.2, stage14.sc.basic, and partials withholding them); for such a person the amount is zero whatever the answers (i1040gi p. 95, Line 20: "If you made contributions to a traditional IRA for 2025, you may be able to take an IRA deduction."), so the reply requires answers the source does not need to determine the result. No value differs. The candidate refusals are other forms' refusals reached through its worksheet for persons with no contribution (mostly a spouse's scveh low_use, s179.multi, scope.other_income, sd.other_forms; refused returns) and its h_se_refused and h_plan_refused declarations; the project refusals are the cited Pub. 590-A refusals (ira.both_kinds, ira.kbh_short, person.ira_over_limit, person.ira_excess_gate, ira.over_comp, ira.special_gate and others on stage16.refuse.*; p590a p. 35). Hardening round re-check: the only project change since fix round 4 is BUG-0263 (person.sep_s3 now links amb.2025.sep_loss_floor; no value change), which this line does not read. Triage executable-triage-v2 (triage/person.json; 1,394 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 2,014 partial records; every witness listed by a scratch rerun of tools/transcription/triage.mjs with the witness cap lifted, counts identical to the record): 2,518 of 4,728 comparisons agree; 10 project-refuses, 245 candidate-refuses, 1,955 candidate-unknown; on returns the full interview completes: 175 candidate-unknown.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; i8606 p. 2, Who Must File: "You made nondeductible contributions to a traditional IRA for 2025" and "You received distributions from a traditional IRA in 2025 and your basis in these IRAs is more than zero." The reply tests both conditions as before (the project screens a distribution with basis at retirement.special), but through person.ira_nondeductible it still needs the worksheet's answers for a person who made no traditional contribution (ira_work_plan, ira_excess, ira_basis, ira_dist, plan, plan_screen and se_screen). rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; i8606 p. 2, Who Must File: "You made nondeductible contributions to a traditional IRA for 2025" and "You received distributions from a traditional IRA in 2025 and your basis in these IRAs is more than zero." The candidate adds the second condition; the project's line serves Form 8606 Part I for nondeductible contributions and a distribution with basis is screened by retirement.special. No value differs. rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; i1040gi p. 97, line 1: "If you checked “No” on line 1a (and “No” on line 1b if married filing jointly), skip lines 2 through 6"; line 2: "Single, head of household, or married filing separately and you lived apart from your spouse for all of 2025, enter $89,000" ... "Married filing jointly, enter $146,000 in both columns. But if you checked “No” on either line 1a or 1b, enter $246,000 for the person who wasn't covered by a plan." The reply changed: it now chooses on its person.ira_cov first (covered: the filing-status amount; not covered: $246,000 for any status) and refuses a separate return living apart (person.h_ira_apart). Value records (checked on each witness): 1,471 are persons covered on neither side on a return where no one is covered (single, head of household, qualifying surviving spouse, or a separate return the project refuses at scope.ready; project $89,000.00, $146,000.00 or $10,000.00 against $246,000.00; 501 on completed returns, for example classm.f4952.1.deepseek, classm.s3.2.deepseek, classm.u1250.2.deepseek), where line 1 skips lines 2 to 6 and ira.anyone_covered is false in both graphs, so no printed line reads the value; the other 164 are joint-return persons the candidate covers through its person.plan reading (amb.2025.ira_covered, ruled at person.ira_cov; $246,000.00 against $146,000.00; 124 completed, classm.f8889.1.deepseek spouse, classm.clcw26.2.deepseek, classm.f8880.2.deepseek). Every value record is on a return with no traditional IRA contribution (ira.any_trad false, or unknown on partials withholding sav_trad, plus stage16.refuse.ira.se_capital, refused), and lines 7a, 7b, 12a, 12b and Schedule 1 line 20 are equal in both graphs wherever both evaluate. But choosing on coverage first makes the line need ira_work_plan (or plan) for every person: all 113 candidate-unknown records on completed returns are persons who answered sav_trad no on returns with no traditional contribution (ira.any_trad false; classm.f8995.3, classm.s179.2, stage14.sc.basic), where the project's line needs no coverage answer and the interview asks none: an answer the source does not need. The 5 candidate refusals are h_ira_apart on separate returns the project refuses (stage10.ss.mfs_apart, generated 165, 306, 406 and 441); project-unknown records withhold ira_work_plan where the candidate's plan answer settles it. Hardening round re-check: the only project change since fix round 4 is BUG-0263 (person.sep_s3 now links amb.2025.sep_loss_floor; no value change), which this line does not read. rulings.ruling: Ruling: ambiguity; amb.2025.ira_covered; i1040gi pp. 97-98, line 7: if no one is covered, enter the applicable amount; otherwise multiply line 6 by the percentage that applies, increase to the next multiple of $10 and enter at least $200. The reply changed: its first branch enters the limit when ira.lines2to6 is false, and that published helper is false when nobody makes a traditional contribution; the project figures the phase-out from coverage alone. So classm.ira.2 (completed, joint, spouse covered by plan sep with a Schedule C, no traditional contribution: project $0.00 after the phase-out, candidate $7,000.00) and classm.sd.2 and .2.deepseek (refused returns) differ in this helper only: line 12 is the smallest of lines 7, 10 and 11, and line 11 is zero, so no deduction differs (representation on that kind). Its tiers are the source's. Project refusals are cited screens reached through the worksheet's modified AGI (person.plan_screened on classm.clcw.4.deepseek and classm.dependent.6.deepseek, oi8z recovery on classm.dependent.1.deepseek, scveh low_use on classm.g28.2), refused returns; project-unknown are partials withholding plan or ira_work_plan (classm.f8889.2.deepseek) where the candidate's limit needs neither; candidate-unknown records lack ira_excess where it is not asked (classm.se.2 spouse, stage14.simple.match_high_comp); the candidate refusal is the excess the project refuses (stage16.refuse.person.ira_excess). The reply changed: it now branches on the published ira.anyone_covered (the applicable limit where no one is covered; zero where line 6 is zero; the limit where line 6 is at or above the threshold; otherwise the reduced amount), where fix round 3's branched on ira.lines2to6. The 31 value records on completed returns (and 37 on refused returns) are all project $7,000.00 against $0.00 on returns with no traditional IRA contribution at all (ira.any_trad and ira.lines2to6 false in both graphs), where the candidate's ira.anyone_covered is true only through its person.ira_cov plan reading (amb.2025.ira_covered, ruled there) and its line 6 is zero: printed lines 7a, 7b, 12a, 12b and Schedule 1 line 20 are $0.00 in both graphs on every one (checked on each witness in a scratch rerun; classm.f8889.1.deepseek spouse, classm.s2.3 spouse, classm.f8962.2.deepseek, classm.tcw.15), so only the helper differs. Project refusals are cited screens reached through modified AGI on refused returns (person.plan_screened, person.simple_excess, person.sep_excess, ira.cov_gate); the candidate refusals are other forms' refusals reached through its modified AGI on refused returns (sd.other_forms, retirement bad_code, scope.other_income, s1.uc_unsupported); candidate-unknown records ask plan of a person with no Schedule C on a return with a contribution (stage16.ira.i1 to i3; amb.2025.ira_covered, placement) or eligible_educator, plan_screen and se_screen through modified AGI; project-unknown records are the project's helper needing ira_work_plan on returns with no contribution, where nothing printed reads it. rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; i8606 p. 9, Line 1: subtract worksheet line 12 "from the smaller of line 10 or line 11 of the worksheet". Same formula as the project's, but it drops the person.sav_trad gate that fix round 2's reply had (and the project has, person.ira_has), so for a person who made no traditional IRA contribution it still needs the worksheet's answers (ira_work_plan, ira_excess, ira_age50, plan, plan_screen and se_screen). Of the candidate-unknown records on completed returns, checked on each witness, 873 are persons who answered sav_trad no, where the interview does not ask those questions (classm.f2441.1.deepseek, classm.f8995.2, stage15.f8880.s2) (the other 26 are contributors, stage16.ira.i1 to i10, asked plan, plan_screen, se_screen or eligible_educator where the interview does not ask them: placement, as in fix round 2); for such a person the amount is zero whatever the answers (i1040gi p. 95, Line 20: "If you made contributions to a traditional IRA for 2025, you may be able to take an IRA deduction."), so the reply requires answers the source does not need to determine the result. No value differs. Candidate refusals are those of person.ira_deduction; the project refusals are the cited Pub. 590-A refusals (stage16.refuse.ira.both_kinds, kbh_short, over_limit, over_comp, special, excluded_income). Fix round 3 re-check: the only project change since fix round 2 is BUG-0256 (person.tin: an expired ITIN counts only if renewed by the due date), which this line does not read. Triage executable-triage-v2 (triage/person.json; 1,390 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 2,014 partial records; every witness listed by a scratch rerun of tools/transcription/triage.mjs with the witness cap lifted): 2,518 of 4,724 comparisons agree; 10 project-refuses, 231 candidate-refuses, 1,965 candidate-unknown; on returns the full interview completes: 3 candidate-refuses, 899 candidate-unknown.

Every candidate-unknown record on a completed return (175, checked on each witness) is a person who answered sav_trad no, where the interview does not ask those questions (for example classm.f8995.3, classm.s179.2, stage14.sc.basic, and partials withholding them); for such a person the amount is zero whatever the answers (i1040gi p. 95, Line 20: "If you made contributions to a traditional IRA for 2025, you may be able to take an IRA deduction."), so the reply requires answers the source does not need to determine the result. No value differs. The candidate refusals are other forms' refusals reached through its worksheet for persons with no contribution (mostly a spouse's scveh low_use, s179.multi, scope.other_income, sd.other_forms; refused returns) and its h_se_refused and h_plan_refused declarations; the project refusals are the cited Pub. 590-A refusals (ira.both_kinds, ira.kbh_short, person.ira_over_limit, person.ira_excess_gate, ira.over_comp, ira.special_gate and others on stage16.refuse.*; p590a p. 35). rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; i8606 p. 9, Line 1: subtract worksheet line 12 "from the smaller of line 10 or line 11 of the worksheet". Same formula as the project's (the smaller of ira.line10 and its line 11, less its line 12), changed only in form; through person.ira_deduction it still needs the worksheet's answers for a person who made no traditional contribution (ira_work_plan, ira_excess, plan, plan_screen and se_screen); the project gates on person.ira_has. Of the candidate-unknown records on completed returns, checked on each witness in a scratch rerun, 875 are persons who answered sav_trad no, where the interview does not ask those questions (classm.f2441.1.deepseek, classm.f8995.2, stage15.f8880.s2) (the other 26 are contributors, stage16.ira.i1 to i10, asked plan, plan_screen, se_screen or eligible_educator where the interview does not ask them: placement); for such a person the amount is zero whatever the answers (i1040gi p. 95, Line 20: "If you made contributions to a traditional IRA for 2025, you may be able to take an IRA deduction."), so the reply requires answers the source does not need to determine the result. No value differs. The candidate refusals are other forms' refusals reached through its worksheet for persons with no contribution (scveh low_use, s179.multi, s1.alimony_unsupported; refused returns) and its se_screen placements (classm.f5695.2 and classm.ssb.5 on completed returns); the project refusals are the cited Pub. 590-A refusals (ira.both_kinds, ira.kbh_short, person.ira_over_limit, ira.over_comp, ira.special_gate, person.ira_dist_gate on stage16.refuse.*; p590a p. 35). Fix round 4 re-check: the only project change since fix round 3 is BUG-0259 (person.itin_applied now counts an application to renew an expired ITIN), which this line does not read. Triage executable-triage-v2 (triage/person.json; 1,390 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 2,014 partial records; every witness listed by a scratch rerun of tools/transcription/triage.mjs with the witness cap lifted): 2,450 of 4,724 comparisons agree; 10 project-refuses, 270 candidate-refuses, 1,994 candidate-unknown; on returns the full interview completes: 3 candidate-refuses, 901 candidate-unknown.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; i1040gi p. 97, line 9: "Enter the earned income you (and your spouse if filing jointly) received as a self-employed individual or a partner ... minus any deductions on Schedule 1, lines 15 and 16. If zero or less, enter -0-." Both subtract Schedule 1 lines 15 and 16 from the Schedule C total, floored at zero (amb.2025.ira_se_floor); no value differs. The reply is again built on sc.line31 rather than sc.result; they differ only for a loss with amounts not at risk, which the project refuses at sc.loss_allowed (stage14.refuse.at_risk, the one project refusal; i1040sc p. 15, Line 32, "Be sure to attach Form 6198"). The candidate declares refusals on person.se_screen and person.rrta for every person; the project asks se_screen only of a person with a Schedule C, so the candidate-unknown records are interview records with no Schedule C where it is not asked (classm.f2441.1.deepseek to .5) and the candidate-refuses supply se_screen true for a person with no Schedule C (classm.f5695.2, classm.f5695.2.deepseek and classm.ssb.5 on completed returns, and the partial records built on them; classm.carloan.2, classm.f8959.1 and classm.w2.1.deepseek rrta on refused returns), an answer the interview does not produce for that person (scope on those kinds, as rounds 1 and 2). The project's other refusals are person.plan_screened (classm.clcw.4, classm.dependent.6 and their .deepseek cases) and person.sep_excess (classm.scveh.6, stage14.sep.refuse_excess), cited screens on refused returns. rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; p560 p. 16, chapter 3, Salary reduction contributions: "These contributions must be expressed as a percentage of the employee's compensation", and the catch-up contribution "can't exceed the lesser of ... The excess of the participant's compensation over the salary reduction contributions that aren't catch-up contributions"; i1040gi p. 93, Line 16: "If you were self-employed or a partner, you may be able to take this deduction." Same expression as the prior round. The candidate's SIMPLE test never compares salary reduction contributions with compensation, so it deducts deferrals with no compensation behind them: stage16.sd.line17_no_skips_18 (Schedule C, employer match maximum $0.00, i.e. no compensation; deferral $5,686.54) deducts $5,686.54 where the project refuses at person.simple_excess; likewise gen#39 ($0.08). Without a Schedule C gate it also deducts a plan for a person with no self-employment (classm.sc.1 spouse $3,626.00, classm.se.1, classm.tcw.13, gen#22 $2,174.89, gen#30; plan supplied without a Schedule C, which the interview does not ask). Other kinds: the project's person.plan_screened refusal for a plan with two Schedules C (stage14.plan.refuse_two_businesses; candidate $20,000.00) is a cited screen (p560 p. 7, "only the earned income from that business is considered for that plan"); person.sep_excess (stage14.sep.refuse_excess, candidate $18,587.04; classm.scveh.6) is the cited excess refusal where the candidate caps at Step 21; the candidate's plan_screen and h_simple_bad refusals and plan_screen unknowns for persons without a Schedule C (classm.w2.1.deepseek, classm.f5695.2, classm.f5695.4, classm.s3.2, classm.f2441.1.deepseek) are placement. rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained (as the prior rulings). The second caps the SEP contribution at Step 21 and the SIMPLE salary reductions at ret.simple_limit with no catch-up (it refuses catch-up contributions, its h_simple_catchup) and caps employer contributions; the project enters the contributions, figures catch-up as the deferral above $16,500, and refuses amounts above the limits (person.sep_excess, person.simple_excess, the plan screen), so the caps never bind on a return it completes. The project also enters zero for a person with no Schedule C (person.has_sc) and asks person.plan only then: i1040gi p. 93, Line 16, "If you were self-employed or a partner, you may be able to take this deduction".
